sources.entry: Crunch - Insane(ly slow but wicked good) PNG image optimization.

summary.one_liner: Crunch is a lossy PNG optimizer that reduces file size using pngquant palette reduction and zopflipng compression, available as a command line tool, a macOS GUI app, and a Finder right-click service.
summary.what_it_does: Crunch applies selective bit depth, color type, and color palette reduction, then encodes with zopfli DEFLATE compression via the pngquant and zopflipng tools. The README says this yields much smaller files than lossless approaches at the cost of a modest drop in image quality. It ships as a *nix-style `crunch` command line executable that runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows POSIX environments such as Cygwin or WSL. It also includes a native macOS drag-and-drop GUI app and a "Crunch Image(s)" Finder right-click service. The README includes example photos and illustrations with original and optimized sizes and DSSIM similarity scores, and says continuous benchmarks run in GitHub Actions.
use_cases: shrink PNG files for a website
batch compress PNG screenshots from the command line
drag and drop PNG compression on a Mac
compress selected PNGs from the Finder right-click menu
lossy optimization of illustrations and photos
how_to_run: Install the `crunch` executable with `make` or manually (see the Install documentation).
Run `crunch` with paths to your PNG files as arguments (see the Usage documentation).
Install the Crunch macOS GUI app with Homebrew or the dmg installer from the repository releases.
Drag and drop PNG images onto the Crunch application window.
Install the 'Crunch Image(s)' right-click service with `make` or by drag and drop in Finder.
Select PNGs in Finder, then choose Services > Crunch Image(s).
notable: Lossy PNG optimization that trades a small quality loss for large size reduction
Three front ends: command line executable, native macOS GUI, and Finder right-click service
Examples report DSSIM similarity scores and percent of original size
Continuous benchmark testing in GitHub Actions with a benchmarks directory
caveats: Lossy compression can visibly degrade some images; the README recommends visual checks in production
The project name's tagline describes it as slow, and the README notes heavy compression is aggressive
The GUI and right-click service are macOS-only; the command line tool also runs on Linux and Windows POSIX environments
